html:
The Electorate of Hanover was a German state in the northwest of the Holy Roman Empire, ruled by a branch of the house of Brunswick-Lüneburg, which became one of the electors who chose the emperor in 1692. It is on the map from 1715 to 1815.

In 1714 the elector, George Louis, became King George I of Great Britain, as the nearest Protestant heir. For 123 years Britain and Hanover shared a ruler, which drew Britain into German wars such as the Seven Years' War. The university founded at Göttingen in the 1730s became one of Europe's best.

Napoleon's wars overran Hanover, and it was occupied and passed around. In 1814 it came back as the Kingdom of Hanover. The link with Britain ended in 1837, when Victoria took the British throne but could not inherit Hanover as a woman. In 1866 Prussia annexed it.
